newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares hit new high on Ericsson, dollar.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares hit new high on Ericsson, dollar.

text.p: Large gains for telecommunications group Ericsson and a strong dollar lifted Swedish shares to a new all-time high on Wednesday.
Capital flows also helped the market, dealers said.
The general index leaped 1.82 percent to a new record high of 2,428.84 in a relatively large turnover of 6.93 billion crowns.

"Everyone is looking for shares now," a trader said. He said part of the reason was that many private investors have cash to spend after selling a certain kind of mutual fund, Allemansfonder, for tax reasons before the New Year.
Ericsson was the most traded share and surged 6.7 percent, or 14 crowns, to 222 crowns on the back of Finnish rival Nokia and U.S. rival Motorola being upgraded by two firms.
The forestry sector kept going strong on a firmer dollar and relief that pulp prices rather seem to be on an uptrend than a downtrend. The sector rose 2.04 percent.
Forestry group MoDo rose 5.50 crowns to 204.50, while SCA rose 2.50 to 145 and Stora advanced 2.50 to 98.00 crowns.
Automotive group Volvo climbed 4.50 crowns to 157 on the dollar and in a rebound after lagging for a while.
